# gstack Builder Ethos

These are the principles that shape how gstack thinks, recommends, and builds.
Skill preambles carry condensed forms of some of them (completeness, voice,
search before building), and the Search Before Building section points here for
the full text. They reflect what we believe about building software in 2026.

---

## The Golden Age

A single person with AI can now build what used to take a team of twenty.
The engineering barrier is gone. What remains is taste, judgment, and the
willingness to do the complete thing.

This is not a prediction — it's happening right now. 10,000+ usable lines of
code per day. 100+ commits per week. Not by a team. By one person, part-time,
using the right tools. The compression ratio between human-team time and
AI-assisted time ranges from 3x (research) to 100x (boilerplate):

| Task type                   | Human team | AI-assisted | Compression |
|-----------------------------|-----------|-------------|-------------|
| Boilerplate / scaffolding   | 2 days    | 15 min      | ~100x       |
| Test writing                | 1 day     | 15 min      | ~50x        |
| Feature implementation      | 1 week    | 30 min      | ~30x        |
| Bug fix + regression test   | 4 hours   | 15 min      | ~20x        |
| Architecture / design       | 2 days    | 4 hours     | ~5x         |
| Research / exploration      | 1 day     | 3 hours     | ~3x         |

This table changes everything about how you make build-vs-skip decisions.
The last 10% of completeness that teams used to skip? It costs seconds now.

---

## 1. Boil the Ocean

"Don't boil the ocean" was the right advice when engineering time was the
bottleneck. That era is over. AI-assisted coding makes the marginal cost of
completeness near-zero, so the old caution has quietly turned into an excuse.
When the complete implementation costs minutes more than the shortcut — do the
complete thing. Every time.

**Ocean, lakes first:** The ocean is the destination — 100% test coverage for a
module, full feature implementation, all edge cases, complete error paths. You
get there one lake at a time: each lake is a boilable unit, not the ceiling.
"That's boiling the ocean" is no longer a reason to ship a shortcut — boiling
the ocean is the goal. The only thing still out of scope is genuinely unrelated
work: a multi-quarter platform migration that has nothing to do with the task at
hand. Flag that as separate scope. Boil everything else.

**Completeness is cheap.** When evaluating "approach A (full, ~150 LOC) vs
approach B (90%, ~80 LOC)" — always prefer A. The 70-line delta costs
seconds with AI coding. "Ship the shortcut" is legacy thinking from when
human engineering time was the bottleneck.

**Anti-patterns:**
- "Choose B — it covers 90% with less code." (If A is 70 lines more, choose A.)
- "Let's defer tests to a follow-up PR." (Tests are the cheapest lake to boil.)
- "This would take 2 weeks." (Say: "2 weeks human / ~1 hour AI-assisted.")

# Working plan: deterministic skill-list ordering

Source: PLAN.md in the fixture repo (commit 9b45bea "Seed review plan").
Review: /plan-ceo-review, mode-only handoff requested by the user. The
substantive review (Sections 1–11, outputs, report) is deliberately NOT run in
this invocation; the user will run it later.

## Plan under review (verbatim from PLAN.md)

Users compare skill listings in scripts and reviews. Make the existing listing
path sort registered skill names deterministically before rendering them.
Keep skill membership, aliases, metadata and text/JSON output formats unchanged.
Cover mixed-case names and differing directory enumeration order with tests.

## Review depth

Implementation-ready (default; the user did not ask for strategy-only or a
single narrow decision). Stated limits recorded from the plan:

| Measure | Value | Unit | Prerequisite |
|---|---|---|---|
| Skill membership | unchanged | set of registered names | existing registry |
| Aliases | unchanged | mapping | existing registry |
| Metadata | unchanged | per-skill fields | existing registry |
| Output formats | unchanged | text and JSON | existing renderers |
| Ordering | deterministic | sort of registered names before render | existing listing path |
| Tests | required | mixed-case names; differing directory enumeration order | test harness |

## Pre-review system audit

- Platform: unknown (no `origin` remote). Base branch: `main` (git-native fallback).
- History: one commit, `9b45bea Seed review plan`. No stash. No TODO/FIXME/HACK markers.
- Repo contents: `CLAUDE.md`, `PLAN.md` only. The listing code the plan modifies is
  not present in this fixture, so code-level leverage below is stated as unknowns
  for the implementation owner to confirm.
- TODOS.md: absent. No prior deferrals.
- Design doc: none found. User is handling /office-hours separately; offer not made.
- Retrospective check: no prior review refactors or reverts (single commit).
- DESIGN_SCOPE: none. CLI text/JSON listing only; no UI screens or components. Section 11 skips.
- Taste calibration: not applicable (recommended mode is HOLD SCOPE, not an expansion mode).
- Prior learnings: cross_project_learnings=false; 0 project learnings found.
- Brain context: all four digests cold (no product, goals, recent-decisions, user-profile).
- Landscape check: Aside not installed (NEEDS_ASIDE); ran one read-only WebSearch.
  - [Layer 1] Tried and true: never rely on readdir/listdir/glob order; apply an
    explicit sort; sort bytewise (codepoint or `LC_ALL=C`) so locale collation
    cannot change results. Source: reproducible-builds.org "Stable order for inputs"
    and "Commandments".
  - [Layer 2] Search results: Python glob deliberately stays unsorted (bpo-30461);
    systemd and mono both landed "sort the input file list" fixes; disorderfs and
    reprotest exist to shuffle/reverse directory order in CI to catch exactly this bug.
  - [Layer 3] First principles: the plan says "deterministic", not "alphabetical".
    Those differ for mixed case. Codepoint order (`Zeta` before `alpha`) is
    deterministic and locale-free but reads oddly; case-insensitive order needs a
    stable tiebreak (e.g. fold then raw) or two names differing only by case
    produce enumeration-dependent output again. This is the one real design
    choice inside the plan and belongs to the implementation review, not mode
    selection. No eureka to log.

## Step 0 ledger

| ID and owner | Contract and evidence | Current | Proposed | Status | Exact approval and scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S0-PREMISE (user) | PLAN.md lines 3–6: listings are diffed by scripts and reviewers; nondeterministic order creates false diffs | Listing renders names in registry/enumeration order (unverified: code not in fixture) | Sort registered names before render; membership, aliases, metadata, formats unchanged | approved (plan as stated) | PLAN.md as handed over; no change proposed by this review |
| S0-COLLATION (implementation owner) | Plan requires mixed-case test coverage; "deterministic" does not specify codepoint vs case-insensitive order | unknown | pending: codepoint sort vs case-folded sort with raw tiebreak | unresolved | Not a Step 0 approach choice; defer to Review Sections (implementation-ready depth). No approval requested here |
| S0-MODE (user) | 0E recommendation; preference check `plan-ceo-review-mode` returned AUTO_DECIDE | none selected | HOLD SCOPE | approved (auto-decided) | Preference check exit 0 AUTO_DECIDE; see handoff provenance below |

### 0A. Premise Challenge

Real problem: two runs of the same listing can print the same skills in different
order because the registry is populated from directory enumeration, which POSIX
leaves unspecified. Target outcome: identical input produces byte-identical text
and JSON listings, so `diff`, snapshot tests and review comments stop flagging
noise. Do-nothing cost: every script that compares listings needs its own
`sort`, and JSON consumers that compare arrays cannot. The plan solves the pain
directly (it fixes the producer, not each consumer). It is not a proxy fix.

### 0B. Existing Code Leverage

| Sub-problem | Reusable code | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Collect registered names | existing registry / listing path | Reuse as-is; plan says "existing listing path" |
| Sort | standard library sort | Reuse ladder rung 2; no new dependency |
| Render text/JSON | existing renderers | Unchanged by contract |
| Simulate enumeration order in tests | existing test harness fixtures | Owner must confirm whether a fake directory walker or injected name list exists |

No rebuild proposed. The fixture repo contains no code, so the implementation
owner must confirm the listing entry point and test helpers.

### 0C. Dream State Mapping

```
  CURRENT STATE                      THIS PLAN                       12-MONTH IDEAL
  Listing order follows      --->    Names sorted once at the   ---> Every user-facing
  readdir order; scripts             listing boundary; text          enumeration (skills,
  and reviews see spurious           and JSON stable; tests          aliases, any future
  diffs between machines             pin mixed-case and              catalog) is sorted at
  and runs                           shuffled enumeration            the producer; CI shuffles
                                                                     directory order to prove it
```

The plan moves toward the ideal. It is the first and smallest lake: one boundary,
one sort, two test classes.

### 0D. Alternatives

No required approach choice. The plan names a single, bounded approach (sort at
the existing listing path) with explicit invariants. The only open design question
(S0-COLLATION) is an implementation detail inside that approach and is recorded
as pending for the Review Sections. No new approach decision was needed.

### 0E. Mode Selection

Planned changed files (estimate; code not in fixture): 1 source edit on the
listing path + 1 test file edit or addition = ~2 files. Category: fix/refactor
of existing behavior with pinned invariants. Not >15 files; category is clear.

Recommendation: HOLD SCOPE because the plan explicitly freezes membership,
aliases, metadata and both output formats, so the value here is rigor on the
one changed behavior (collation rule, locale independence, case-only collisions,
shuffled-enumeration tests) rather than any new capability.

Preference check: `gstack-question-preference --check plan-ceo-review-mode`
exited 0 with AUTO_DECIDE. Per 0E step 3 the recommendation is selected without
a question. Selected mode: HOLD SCOPE.

## Route after mode

HOLD SCOPE route is 0G → 0I → Review Sections. Per the user's instruction this
invocation stops after the mode handoff. 0G, 0I and Review Sections 1–11,
required outputs and the GSTACK REVIEW REPORT are pending for the later run.

## NOT in scope

Nothing cut or deferred by this invocation.
